Conclusion

After completing these steps, the Debian 13 server is ready for development, programming, Docker, AI tools, and basic server hosting.

The most important things are not only installing software. You can also need to take care of security, SSH access, firewall rules, passwords, disk space, RAM, Docker logs, and system updates.

This setup may gives you a simple and practical development server that you can use for coding, AI experiments, Docker projects, and personal services.

 

 

Some Useful Linux Websites You Might Use

Here are some websites that I often find useful when working with Linux servers.

1. Linux Documentation

Linux man-pages

Useful for learning Linux commands and system functions.

Linux man-pages

2. Debian Documentation

The official Debian documentation is useful when working with Debian servers.

Debian Documentation

It includes installation guides, system administration information, and Debian manuals.

3. Debian Packages

When I want to check whether a package is available in Debian, I can use the Debian Packages website.

Debian Packages

4. Ubuntu Documentation

Even when I am using Debian, Ubuntu documentation can sometimes be useful because many Linux commands and concepts are similar.

Ubuntu Documentation

5. Linux Journey

Linux Journey is a beginner-friendly website for learning Linux.

Linux Journey

It covers topics such as:

Command line

Permissions

Processes

Networking

File systems

Shell scripting

6. ExplainShell

When I find a complicated Linux command, ExplainShell can help me understand it.

Docker Documentation

Docker

14. ArchWiki

Even if I am not using Arch Linux, the ArchWiki is one of the best Linux references available.
